questionsToConsider: Which wheel sizes, brake mounts and axle standards do you actually stock?
Who in the shop will look at the photos riders send, and how quickly can they reply?
Do you want an extra result for e-bikes or cargo bikes if you sell wheels for them?
Should riders who pick high end see an offer to book a fitting or a test ride?
guide.howToUseResponses: Start with the rows that include a photo or a "Not sure" answer, since those riders need a person to confirm compatibility before they buy anything. For everyone else, the wheel size, brake and axle answers let you filter your stock to the wheels that fit. Export to CSV to see which riding result is most common and plan stock around it.
customizeSteps: Edit the wheel size, brake and axle options to match the standards in your range.
Rename each result after the wheelsets you'd genuinely recommend and add their key specs.
Put the quiz on your wheels page and share the link when riders ask what will fit.

faqs.q: How do I know which bike wheels will fit my bike?
faqs.a: You need the wheel size, the brake type (rim or disc) and the axle type, such as quick release or thru-axle. The tyre sidewall usually shows the size, and a bike shop can confirm the rest.

faqs.q: What happens when a rider doesn't know their brake type?
faqs.a: The quiz asks for a photo of the wheel's centre and brake, so someone at your shop can check it before recommending anything.

faqs.q: How does the quiz choose between road, gravel, mountain and commuter wheels?
faqs.a: The final question about where they ride routes each rider to one of four results. You can edit the options and rewrite each result for your own wheelsets.

endings.title: A durable commuter wheelset 🏙️
endings.bodyMd: For daily riding, a strong wheel with more spokes and reliable sealed bearings will outlast lighter options and needs less truing. Pair it with puncture-resistant tyres and it'll handle potholes and kerbs for years.

endings.title: A lightweight road wheelset 🚴
endings.bodyMd: Lighter rims spin up faster and deeper profiles hold speed on flat roads, which is where road wheels earn their money. We'll match the brake type and axle you gave us, and suggest a stronger build if you're carrying extra load.

endings.title: A tough, wide gravel wheelset 🪨
endings.bodyMd: Wider rims support bigger tyres at lower pressure, which means more grip and comfort on rough surfaces. Tubeless-ready gravel wheels also shrug off the small punctures that come with it.

endings.title: A trail-ready mountain bike wheelset 🌲
endings.bodyMd: Trail wheels need to take hits more than save grams, so look for strong rims, a solid hub and tubeless compatibility. We'll check your wheel size and axle standard before suggesting a pair.
